Reproducing Ghaderi, Crochet & Petersen (2026) from dandiset 001530: behaviour, optogenetics and single-neuron analyses¶

Paper. Ghaderi P, Crochet S, Petersen CCH (2026). Contextual gating of whisker-evoked responses by frontal cortex supports flexible decision making. Nature Communications 17, 5982. doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73622-y. The claims file was written from the version of record in Europe PMC (PMC13346651): main text, legends and Methods; the Supplementary Information was not read by the reader.

Dandiset. DANDI:001530, version 0.260605.0601. The paper cites the dandiset without a version. This is the only published version and the most recent one; the draft has the same 196 assets and the same size (2,595,454,486,752 bytes), and it was last modified within seconds of the publication (2026-06-05), so nothing in the draft is newer than what is pinned here.

What is read. The 35 *-processed-behavior.nwb files (Neuropixels units with Allen CCF labels, trials, DeepLabCut traces) and the 91 *-opto-behavior.nwb files (trials of the optogenetic sessions), streamed from the archive. The *-processed-behavior-raw.nwb files and the videos hold the raw voltage and video of the same sessions and are not needed here.

Outside inputs (Zenodo record doi:10.5281/zenodo.17973874, the paper's data and code, read by range requests into memory): data_helpers/Area_list.mat, the CCF labels that make up each of the five areas, and processed_data/Data_Clustering.mat, the paper's cluster label for each neuron (claims cluster-label-link and fig4b-named-clusters), and data_helpers/Lick_times.mat, the detected lick times and lick mask (claims fig8b-lick-coding-direction and figs18-later-lick-coding), fetched by parallel range requests.

The population decoding claims and the clustering of Figure 4a are in decoding_delay.ipynb and decoding_clusters_whisker.ipynb.

import time
import warnings
import collections
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import ghaderi as g

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)
pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 300)

started = time.time()
print(f"dandiset {g.DANDISET_ID} version {g.DANDISET_VERSION}: {len(g.assets())} assets")
AREA_LIST = g.area_list()
S = g.load_sessions(workers=4)
print(f"loaded {len(S)} ephys sessions in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")
t0 = time.time()
O = g.load_opto()
print(f"loaded {len(O)} optogenetic sessions in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

kinds = collections.Counter()
for path, size, _ in g.assets():
    kind = ("ephys processed" if path.endswith("-processed-behavior.nwb") else
            "ephys raw" if path.endswith("-raw.nwb") else
            "video" if path.endswith(".avi") else
            "optogenetics" if path.endswith("-opto-behavior.nwb") else "other")
    kinds[kind] += 1
print("Assets by kind:", dict(kinds))
print("Subjects with ephys:", sorted({s["subject"] for s in S}), "n =", len({s["subject"] for s in S}))
print("Subjects with optogenetics:", sorted({o["subject"] for o in O}), "n =", len({o["subject"] for o in O}))
print("All subjects:", len({s["subject"] for s in S} | {o["subject"] for o in O}), "(archive summary: 21)")
print("\nCCF labels per area (Area_list.mat):")
for a, labels in AREA_LIST.items():
    print(f"  {a}: {len(labels)} labels, e.g. {labels[0].strip()!r}")

rows = []
for s in S:
    tr, c = s["trials"], s["completed"]
    tt = tr["trial_type"]
    rows.append({"session": s["session"], "subject": s["subject"], "trials": len(tt),
                 "completed": int(c.sum()), "early_lick": int((~c).sum()),
                 **{f"type{k}": int(((tt == k) & c).sum()) for k in range(0, 6)},
                 "units": len(s["units"]["location"]), "analysed_units": len(s["keep"]),
                 "probes": ",".join(sorted(set(s["units"]["location"]))),
                 "video_dt_ms": round(s["beh_info"]["video_dt_median_ms"], 3),
                 "unsorted_units": s["unsorted_units"]})
info = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(info.to_string(index=False))
print("\nTrial type 0 (not one of the five types) in:", info.loc[info.type0 > 0, "session"].tolist())
print("Sessions without No-tone Whisker trials:", info.loc[info.type5 == 0, "session"].tolist())
print("Units whose spike times are not sorted:", int(info.unsorted_units.sum()))

The archive lists 21 subjects: 14 mice with recordings and 15 with optogenetics, with overlap. The 35 recording sessions in 14 mice are the paper's (Results; the Methods' list sums to 34). Two sessions break the five trial types: one has 11 trials coded trial_type 0, and one has no No-tone trials; both are kept, with type 0 excluded from every trial type. Video frame intervals are 5 ms (200 frames/s) in every session except the two of PG019, at 10 ms, as the Methods say (100 Hz in PG019).

The whisker stimulus is 1.0 s after start_time in every trial and the first lick falls in the 1 s response window (1 to 2 s), as the Methods describe. whisker_stim_duration is 0.01 s, the 10 ms cosine pulse of the Methods (5 ms at half maximum). Each mouse has one Go and one Nogo frequency (4 or 8 kHz).

Whisker angle is in degrees and jaw and tongue in pixels, as the files state. Video covers almost every trial: every session has at least one trial without video frames in its -1 to 2 s window (the total is printed above), and two have many, 243 trials in sub-PG061_ses-20220212T233813 and 29 in sub-PG038_ses-20210316T152753. Those trials cannot pass the quiet rule and are counted as not quiet, as the paper's code counts them (a NaN fails its comparison; quiet-trials-half below).

# Shared clock of spikes and trials: whisker-evoked response (1.00 to 1.03 s) in whisker against
# no-whisker trials, in wS1 and wS2, with true and with trial labels shifted by one trial.
rows = []
w, b = g.bin_index(1.01, 1.03), g.bin_index(0.8, 1.0)
for k, s in enumerate(S):
    tt = s["trials"]["trial_type"][s["completed"]]
    whisk = np.isin(tt, [1, 3, 5])
    for a in ("wS1", "wS2", "A1", "all units"):
        cols = np.arange(len(s["keep"])) if a == "all units" else g.area_columns(s, a)
        if len(cols) < 5:
            continue
        x = s["c10"][:, :, cols].astype(float)
        if a == "A1":   # auditory response 0 to 30 ms, tone against no-tone trials
            resp = x[:, g.bin_index(0.01, 0.03)].mean(axis=(1, 2)) - x[:, g.bin_index(-0.2, 0.0)].mean(axis=(1, 2))
            lab = np.isin(tt, [1, 2, 3, 4])
        else:
            resp = x[:, w].mean(axis=(1, 2)) - x[:, b].mean(axis=(1, 2))
            lab = whisk
        rows.append({"session": s["session"], "area": a,
                     "contrast_true": (resp[lab].mean() - resp[~lab].mean()) / g.W10,
                     "contrast_shifted": (resp[np.roll(lab, 1)].mean() - resp[~np.roll(lab, 1)].mean()) / g.W10})
clock = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Stimulus-evoked change in rate (Hz per neuron), stimulus minus no-stimulus trials:")
print(clock.groupby("area")[["contrast_true", "contrast_shifted"]].describe().round(2).T.to_string())
print("\nArea-sessions where the true contrast is not above the shifted one:")
print(clock[clock.contrast_true <= clock.contrast_shifted].to_string(index=False))
print("Sessions with no wS1, wS2 or A1 area of 5 units (checked with all units only):",
      sorted(set(clock.session) - set(clock[clock.area != "all units"].session)))
print("Sessions with fewer than 5 analysed units (not checked):", [s["session"] for s in S if len(s["keep"]) < 5])

In every area-session the whisker-evoked response in wS1 and wS2 and the tone-evoked response in A1 are larger in the trials that had the stimulus than in those that did not, and the contrast vanishes when the labels are shifted by one trial (table above). The sessions with only frontal units are checked with all their units pooled (whisker-evoked response, 1.00 to 1.03 s). Spikes and the trial table share a clock in each session tested this way. sub-PG038_ses-20210317T180556 keeps no unit after the CCF filter, so it is not checked and enters only the behavioural claims.

The 91 optogenetic sessions cover the six areas with 9 to 20 sessions each; mice per area are A1 9, wS1 10, wS2 10, wM2 9, ALM 7 and fpS1 8, where the Methods give 8 mice for ALM. Each session inactivates one area in one window. Twelve sessions (mice PG021 and PG061) give the genotype C57BL/6JRj, which carries no ChR2, although the paper inactivates only VGAT-ChR2 mice; their light trials still reduce licking (see fig2 below), so the genotype field is likely wrong for these mice. The trials table describes opto_area as "laser light duration" and opto_stim_start_time as "Pulse duration in s", which do not fit their values.

fig1c-lick-probabilities¶

Mice lick in the response window on 78 +/- 2% of Go-tone Whisker trials and withhold licking in the other trial types (Go-tone No-Whisker 10 +/- 1%, Nogo-tone Whisker 13 +/- 2%, Nogo-tone No-Whisker 1 +/- 0.3%, No-tone Whisker 15 +/- 2%), mean +/- SEM over 35 recording sessions in 14 mice.

As the criterion (code, Ghaderi2025_Figure1_c_Performance.m): completed trials, lick_flag, mean and SEM over sessions.

fig1f-movement-latencies¶

In quiet Hit trials the whisker deflection is followed by whisker protraction (time to 20% of maximum 58 +/- 8 ms), jaw opening (115 +/- 17 ms) and tongue protrusion (231 +/- 29 ms), and tongue-spout contact at 330 +/- 20 ms.

Traces as code, Ghaderi2025_Figure1_f_Movements_Hit.m (quiet completed Hit trials, 10 ms bins, each trial minus its mean over 0.8 to 1.0 s; NaN tongue values set to 0 as the code does). Readings (a) and (b) of the criterion, with the maximum over 1.0 to 2.0 s, the 1 s response window after the whisker stimulus (Methods, Mouse behavior), as the claims file has it since a reader answered the question on the window. The lick latency as Ghaderi2025_Sup_Figure1_b_SpoutReactionTime.m. A latency is the right edge of the first bin after 1.0 s that reaches 20% of the maximum, minus 1.0 s. As variants the maximum is taken over 1.0 to 1.2 s (the Fig. 1f plot window, the criterion's window before the answer) and 1.0 to 1.5 s, and the quiet rule uses the code's mean absolute deviation.

In [9]:
labels10 = g.PRE + g.W10 * np.arange(1, g.N10 + 1)
base_bins = g.bin_index(0.8, 1.0)


def latency_ms(trace, post):
    seg = trace[post]
    mx = np.nanmax(seg) if np.isfinite(seg).any() else np.nan
    if not np.isfinite(mx) or mx <= 0:
        return np.nan
    hit = np.flatnonzero(seg >= 0.2 * mx)
    hit = hit[labels10[post][hit] > 1.0]
    return (labels10[post][hit[0]] - 1.0) * 1000 if len(hit) else np.nan


def movement_latencies(rule="median", end=2.0):
    post = g.bin_index(1.0, end)
    out = []
    for s in S:
        sel = g.trial_mask(s, 1, True) & g.quiet_mask(s, rule)
        row = {"session": s["session"], "subject": s["subject"], "n_trials": int(sel.sum())}
        for sigl in ("whisker_speed", "jaw_movement", "tongue_movement"):
            x = s["beh"][sigl][s["completed"]][sel].copy()
            if sigl == "tongue_movement":
                x = np.where(np.isnan(x), 0, x)
            x = x - np.nanmean(x[:, base_bins], axis=1, keepdims=True)
            row[f"{sigl}_a"] = latency_ms(np.nanmean(x, axis=0), post) if len(x) else np.nan
            row[f"{sigl}_b"] = np.nanmean([latency_ms(t, post) for t in x]) if len(x) else np.nan
        out.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


lick_rows = []
for s in S:
    tr, c = s["trials"], s["completed"]
    rt = tr["lick_time"] - tr["start_time"]
    rt[(rt > 2) | (rt < 1)] = np.nan
    hit = (tr["trial_type"] == 1) & tr["lick_flag"].astype(bool) & c
    lick_rows.append(np.nanmean((rt - 1)[hit]) * 1000)
lick = np.array(lick_rows)
print(f"Lick latency (all completed Hit trials): {lick.mean():.1f} +/- {lick.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(lick)):.1f} ms "
      f"(n = {len(lick)} sessions; paper 330 +/- 20)")


def summarise(df, label):
    rows = []
    for sigl, (v, tol) in {"whisker_speed": (58, 8), "jaw_movement": (115, 17), "tongue_movement": (231, 29)}.items():
        for r in "ab":
            x = df[f"{sigl}_{r}"].dropna()
            rows.append({"variant": label, "signal": sigl, "reading": r, "sessions": len(x),
                         "mean ms": round(x.mean(), 1), "SEM": round(x.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(x)), 1),
                         "paper": f"{v} +/- {tol}", "within": abs(x.mean() - v) <= tol})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

for sigl, col in zip(("whisker_speed", "jaw_movement", "tongue_movement"), ("m", "c", "orange")):
    traces = []
    for s in S:
        sel = g.trial_mask(s, 1, True) & g.quiet_mask(s)
        if sel.sum() == 0:
            continue
        x = s["beh"][sigl][s["completed"]][sel].copy()
        if sigl == "tongue_movement":
            x = np.where(np.isnan(x), 0, x)
        x = x - np.nanmean(x[:, base_bins], axis=1, keepdims=True)
        traces.append(np.nanmean(x, axis=0)[g.bin_index(0.8, 2.0)])
    m = np.nanmean(traces, axis=0)
    ax.plot(t, m / np.nanmax(m), color=col, label=sigl)
    print(f"{sigl}: grand-mean trace, max at {t[np.nanargmax(m)]:.2f} s; normalised range {np.nanmin(m / np.nanmax(m)):.2f} to 1")
ax.axvline(1.0, color="k", lw=0.5)
ax.axvline(1.2, color="grey", ls="--", lw=0.5)  # end of the Fig. 1f plot and of the 1.2 s variant
ax.set_xlabel("time from trial start (s)")
ax.set_ylabel("movement / max")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.show()

jaw_movement: grand-mean trace, max at 1.34 s; normalised range -0.00 to 1
tongue_movement: grand-mean trace, max at 1.35 s; normalised range 0.00 to 1

Result: partially reproduced. The lick latency is 330.1 +/- 20.2 ms, as the paper reports. With the maximum over 1.0 to 2.0 s, as the claims file now has it, reading (a) gives whisker 54.4, jaw 115.3 and tongue 192.4 ms and reading (b) 94.6, 142.9 and 254.6 ms, against 58, 115 and 231 ms. Under reading (a) the whisker and jaw latencies are within tolerance and the tongue latency is 38.6 ms short of 231, outside the 29 ms tolerance; under reading (b) only the tongue latency is within tolerance. The order whisker, jaw, tongue, spout contact holds under both readings, so both give the criterion's partial case. The session means are pulled up by a few late sessions: the medians over sessions under reading (a) are 50.0, 95.0 and 155.0 ms, and the two PG019 sessions average a jaw latency of 315.0 ms and a tongue latency of 385.0 ms. With the maximum over 1.0 to 1.2 s (the window before the reader's answer) no movement latency under reading (a) and only the whisker latency under reading (b) is within tolerance, and with the code's mean absolute deviation for the quiet rule the values are close to the criterion's (50.9, 118.0 and 196.0 ms under reading a).

quiet-trials-half¶

Selecting quiet trials (no whisker or jaw movement in the last 200 ms of the delay) rejects about half of the recorded trials.

# How the paper's code treats trials without video (verifier's question). The code's lines:
print(g.code_lines("functions/nwb_findQuietTrial.m", r"nanmean|TH=|thereshold=TH|ind_quiete=prewhiskvalue<="))

# nanmedian ignores NaN, MATLAB's mad() removes NaN values (its documented behaviour), so the
# threshold is finite; a trial whose pre-stimulus mean is NaN fails "prewhiskvalue <= thereshold".
rows = []
base_bins, pre_bins = g.bin_index(-1.0, 0.0), g.bin_index(0.8, 1.0)
for s in S:
    r = {"session": s["session"], "trials": len(s["completed"])}
    nan_any_base = np.zeros(len(s["completed"]), bool)
    for sig in ("whisker_speed", "jaw_movement"):
        x = s["beh"][sig]
        r[f"NaN baseline {sig}"] = int(np.isnan(x[:, base_bins]).all(axis=1).sum())
        r[f"NaN pre-stimulus {sig}"] = int(np.isnan(x[:, pre_bins]).all(axis=1).sum())
        nan_any_base |= np.isnan(x[:, base_bins]).all(axis=1)
    r["NaN in either"] = int(nan_any_base.sum())
    rows.append(r)
nan_tab = pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: partially reproduced. With the Methods' rule (median absolute deviation) the quiet selection rejects 55.06% of the completed trials (pooled; median over sessions 53.3%) and 56.72% of all trials, just outside the 45 to 55% tolerance under both readings and inside the 30 to 70% band for a partial result. With the code's mean absolute deviation, 40.22% of completed trials are rejected. Leaving out the trials without video gives 54.22%. Counting those trials as not quiet is the code's rule: nwb_findQuietTrial.m takes nanmedian and mad() (which drops NaN) for the threshold and compares the NaN pre-stimulus mean with <=, which fails (lines printed above). Every session has at least one trial with a NaN baseline, so a threshold that kept NaN would reject every trial.

Optogenetic inactivation (Figure 2)¶

Per session, P(lick) over completed Go-tone Whisker trials with no light and with light in the session's window (code, Ghaderi2025_Figure2_d_Plick_Sessions.m). The reduction is the mean over sessions of no-light minus light P(lick), in points (reading a), or as percent of no-light P(lick) (reading b). The test draws 9 sessions with replacement (the smallest session count over areas and windows, computed below), p = (draws on the wrong side + 1) / iterations, two-tailed, Benjamini-Hochberg over the six areas within a window; 1,000 iterations (Methods) and 10,000 (code). The spread is given as SEM and SD over sessions.

In [13]:
def plick(o, window, ttype=1):
    tr = o["trials"]
    sel = ~tr["early_lick"].astype(bool) & (tr["trial_type"] == ttype) & (tr["opto_window"] == window)
    return 100 * tr["lick_flag"][sel].mean() if sel.any() else np.nan


WINDOWS = ["audio", "delay", "whisker"]


def opto_pairs(ttype=1):
    out = {}
    for a in g.OPTO_AREAS:
        sess = [o for o in O if o["area"] == a]
        nl = np.array([plick(o, "nolight", ttype) for o in sess])
        for w_ in WINDOWS:
            op = np.array([plick(o, w_, ttype) for o in sess])
            ok = np.isfinite(op) & np.isfinite(nl)
            out[a, w_] = (nl[ok], op[ok], [sess[i]["subject"] for i in np.flatnonzero(ok)])
    return out


pairs = opto_pairs()
n_draw = min(len(v[0]) for v in pairs.values())
print("Smallest number of sessions over areas and windows:", n_draw)
opto_rows = []
for iterations in (1000, 10000):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
    for w_ in WINDOWS:
        ps = [g.paired_bootstrap_p(pairs[a, w_][0], pairs[a, w_][1], n_draw, iterations, rng) for a in g.OPTO_AREAS]
        qs = g.bh_fdr(ps)
        for a, p_, q_ in zip(g.OPTO_AREAS, ps, qs):
            nl, op, subj = pairs[a, w_]
            d = nl - op
            opto_rows.append({"iterations": iterations, "window": w_, "area": a, "sessions": len(d), "mice": len(set(subj)),
                              "reduction_pts": d.mean(), "SEM": d.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(d)), "SD": d.std(ddof=1),
                              "relative_%": 100 * np.mean(d / nl), "p": p_, "p_FDR": q_})
opto_tab = pd.DataFrame(opto_rows)
print(opto_tab.round(4).to_string(index=False))

Result: reproduced (fig2-auditory-window). In the Auditory window the reductions are A1 38.9 (SEM 4.1), wM2 33.0 (5.7), wS2 26.0 (3.8) and wS1 19.5 (6.1) points, all within tolerance in points; these four areas are significant after FDR (10,000 iterations: 0.0004, 0.0004, 0.0004 and 0.0021; 1,000: 0.004 to 0.012) and ALM (7.8 points, p 0.161) and fpS1 (0.1, p 0.979) are not. The paper's spread matches the SEM, not the SD. As a percent of no-light P(lick) (reading b) the values are larger and out of tolerance, so the paper's numbers are points.

Result: reproduced (fig2-delay-window). In the Delay window wM2 44.5 (SEM 7.2), ALM 32.1 (5.5) and wS1 16.0 (3.0) points, within tolerance and significant (p_FDR 0.0004 with 10,000 iterations); A1 (7.8, p 0.113), wS2 (8.2, p 0.076) and fpS1 (4.3, p 0.292) are not significant.

Result: reproduced (fig2-whisker-window). In the Whisker window ALM 52.3 (SEM 3.8), wM2 48.2 (3.8), wS1 37.6 (3.5), wS2 35.5 (3.7) and A1 12.8 (3.5) points, within tolerance and significant (p_FDR 0.0003 for the first four and 0.0115 for A1 with 10,000 iterations, the paper's 0.0003 and 0.01); fpS1 (8.7, p 0.118) is not. With 1,000 iterations the pattern is the same.

fig2-wm2-vs-alm-auditory¶

Inactivation during the auditory window reduces licking significantly more for wM2 than for ALM (33 +/- 6% against 8 +/- 5%).

Unpaired bootstrap of the difference of the two areas' mean per-session reductions, readings (a) 9 sessions per area and (b) all sessions of each area, two-tailed with the code's p rule; FDR over the 15 area pairs of the Auditory window as a variant.

In [16]:
def unpaired_bootstrap_p(x, y, n_x, n_y, iterations, rng):
    d = rng.choice(x, (iterations, n_x)).mean(axis=1) - rng.choice(y, (iterations, n_y)).mean(axis=1)
    obs = x.mean() - y.mean()
    p_ = ((d <= 0).sum() + 1) / iterations if obs > 0 else ((d >= 0).sum() + 1) / iterations
    return 2 * min(p_, 1 - p_)


red = {a: pairs[a, "audio"][0] - pairs[a, "audio"][1] for a in g.OPTO_AREAS}
print(f"wM2 {red['wM2'].mean():.1f} +/- {red['wM2'].std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(red['wM2'])):.1f} (n {len(red['wM2'])}); "
      f"ALM {red['ALM'].mean():.1f} +/- {red['ALM'].std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(red['ALM'])):.1f} (n {len(red['ALM'])})")
for iterations in (1000, 10000):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
    pa = unpaired_bootstrap_p(red["wM2"], red["ALM"], 9, 9, iterations, rng)
    pb = unpaired_bootstrap_p(red["wM2"], red["ALM"], len(red["wM2"]), len(red["ALM"]), iterations, rng)
    pairs15 = [(a, b) for i, a in enumerate(g.OPTO_AREAS) for b in g.OPTO_AREAS[i + 1:]]
    pall = [unpaired_bootstrap_p(red[a], red[b], len(red[a]), len(red[b]), iterations, rng) for a, b in pairs15]
    q15 = g.bh_fdr(pall)[pairs15.index(("wM2", "ALM"))]
    print(f"{iterations} iterations: reading (a) p = {pa:.4f}; reading (b) p = {pb:.4f}; "
          f"(b) with FDR over the 15 pairs: {q15:.4f}")

wM2 33.0 +/- 5.7 (n 14); ALM 7.8 +/- 5.4 (n 9)
1000 iterations: reading (a) p = 0.0060; reading (b) p = 0.0020; (b) with FDR over the 15 pairs: 0.0050
10000 iterations: reading (a) p = 0.0024; reading (b) p = 0.0008; (b) with FDR over the 15 pairs: 0.0018

Result: reproduced. wM2 33.0 +/- 5.7 and ALM 7.8 +/- 5.4 points, both within tolerance, and the bootstrap gives p < 0.05 with wM2 larger under both readings (10,000 iterations: 0.0024 and 0.0008 uncorrected, 0.0018 after FDR over the 15 pairs; 1,000 iterations: 0.006, 0.002 and 0.005).

units-recorded¶

Across 35 sessions in 14 mice, 10,294 well-isolated units were recorded in the five areas (A1 780, wS1 1938, wS2 2064, wM2 2749, ALM 2763).

The files hold only the units kept after curation (no inclusion column); a unit is in an area when its probe location is the area and its ccf_location is one of the area's labels in Area_list.mat.

fig3a-activity-maps¶

In quiet Hit trials, probe-averaged activity changes are largest in A1 in the first 30 ms after the tone, in wM2 and ALM in the last 200 ms of the delay, in wS1 and wS2 in the first 30 ms after the whisker deflection, and in frontal areas 300 to 500 ms after it.

Per area-session (one probe each), the mean over neurons of the trial-averaged change in rate over quiet Hit trials in the windows of the code (Ghaderi2025_Figure3_a_brainmap_activity.m, bins labelled 0.01-0.03, 0.8-1.0, 1.01-1.03 and 1.3-1.5 s); per area, the mean over probes. Pre-whisker baseline readings (a) 0.95 to 1.0 s and (b) 0.8 to 1.0 s; the code's -1 to 0 s baseline for every window is a variant.

In [19]:
WIN3A = {"Auditory": (0.01, 0.03), "Delay": (0.8, 1.0), "Whisker": (1.01, 1.03), "Lick": (1.3, 1.5)}
TOP = {"Auditory": {"A1"}, "Delay": {"wM2", "ALM"}, "Whisker": {"wS1", "wS2"}, "Lick": {"wM2", "ALM"}}


def activity_maps(reading):
    rows = []
    for a in g.AREAS:
        for s, cols in g.area_sessions(S, a):
            sel = g.trial_mask(s, 1, True) & g.quiet_mask(s)
            if sel.sum() == 0:
                continue
            m = s["c10"][sel][:, :, cols].mean(axis=0) / g.W10
            row = {"area": a, "session": s["session"], "neurons": len(cols), "trials": int(sel.sum())}
            for k, (t1, t2) in WIN3A.items():
                if k in ("Auditory", "Delay") or reading == "code":
                    b = g.bin_index(-1.0, 0.0)
                else:
                    b = g.bin_index(0.95, 1.0) if reading == "a" else g.bin_index(0.8, 1.0)
                row[k] = (m[g.bin_index(t1, t2)].mean(axis=0) - m[b].mean(axis=0)).mean()
            rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


for reading in ("a", "b", "code"):
    df = activity_maps(reading)
    means = df.groupby("area")[list(WIN3A)].mean().loc[g.AREAS]
    print(f"Reading {reading}: mean over probes (Hz)")
    print(means.round(2).to_string())
    held = []
    for k, top in TOP.items():
        order = means[k].sort_values(ascending=False).index.tolist()
        ok = set(order[:len(top)]) == top
        held.append(ok)
        print(f"  {k}: largest {order[:len(top)]}, expected {sorted(top)} -> {ok}")
    print(f"  {sum(held)} of 4 hold\n")
print("Per probe, reading (a):")
print(activity_maps("a").round(2).to_string(index=False))

Result: reproduced. Under both pre-whisker readings, A1 has the largest change in the Auditory window (5.55 Hz against at most 1.54), wM2 and ALM the two largest in the Delay window (0.70 and 0.35 Hz; A1 0.20), wS1 and wS2 the two largest in the Whisker window (6.80 and 5.61 Hz under (a)) and wM2 and ALM the two largest in the Lick window (1.79 and 1.80 Hz under (a); wS2 1.28). The code's -1 to 0 s baseline gives the same ranking.

fig3b-delay-and-response-psth¶

In grand-average PSTHs of correct quiet trials, firing in wM2 and ALM is elevated during the delay of Go-tone trials compared with Nogo-tone trials, and after the whisker stimulus activity rises in Go-tone Whisker Hit trials compared with all other trial types in wS1, wS2, wM2 and ALM.

Per neuron, baseline-subtracted means over quiet correct trials; Wilcoxon signed-rank over neurons. Pooled Go-tone trials are the Hit and Go-tone No-Whisker correct trials together, and likewise for Nogo-tone. Neurons of sessions lacking either condition are left out (counts printed).

In [20]:
hit = lambda s: g.correct_mask(s, 1)
go12 = lambda s: g.correct_mask(s, 1) | g.correct_mask(s, 2)
ng34 = lambda s: g.correct_mask(s, 3) | g.correct_mask(s, 4)
rows = []
for variant, sigs in (("main (whisker and jaw)", ("whisker_speed", "jaw_movement")), ("code (whisker only)", ("whisker_speed",))):
    for a in ("wM2", "ALM"):
        for pairing, (m1, m2) in {"pooled 1+2 vs 3+4": (go12, ng34), "type 1 vs 3": (hit, lambda s: g.correct_mask(s, 3))}.items():
            (x, y), sess = g.neuron_window_means(S, a, [m1, m2], (0.8, 1.0), signals=sigs)
            rows.append({"variant": variant, "part": "i delay", "area": a, "comparison": pairing, "window": "0.8-1.0",
                         "neurons": len(x), "sessions": len(set(sess)), "Go": x.mean(), "other": y.mean(),
                         "diff": (x - y).mean(), "p": stats.wilcoxon(x, y).pvalue})
    for window in ((1.3, 1.5), (1.0, 1.5)):
        for a in ("wS1", "wS2", "wM2", "ALM"):
            for t_ in (2, 3, 4, 5):
                (x, y), sess = g.neuron_window_means(S, a, [hit, lambda s, t_=t_: g.correct_mask(s, t_)], window, signals=sigs)
                rows.append({"variant": variant, "part": "ii response", "area": a, "comparison": f"Hit vs type {t_}",
                             "window": f"{window[0]}-{window[1]}", "neurons": len(x), "sessions": len(set(sess)),
                             "Go": x.mean(), "other": y.mean(), "diff": (x - y).mean(), "p": stats.wilcoxon(x, y).pvalue})
psth = pd.DataFrame(rows)
psth["holds"] = (psth["diff"] > 0) & (psth.p < 0.05)
print(psth.round(4).to_string(index=False))
for (variant, part, window), sub in psth.groupby(["variant", "part", "window"]):
    print(f"{variant}, {part}, {window}: {int(sub.holds.sum())} of {len(sub)} comparisons hold; failing: "
          f"{sub.loc[~sub.holds, ['area', 'comparison']].values.tolist()}")

Result: partially reproduced. (i) holds: in wM2 and ALM delay firing is higher in Go-tone than Nogo-tone trials under both pairings (wM2 p 0.004 pooled and 0.0015 by type; ALM 0.009 and 0.008). (ii) holds in wS1, wM2 and ALM, but in wS2 the Hit response over 1.3 to 1.5 s is not significantly above No-tone Whisker trials (difference 0.80 Hz, p 0.11), so (ii) fails for one area. Over 1.0 to 1.5 s every comparison holds. With the code's whisker-only quiet rule (ii) fails for the same wS2 comparison and (i) also fails for ALM by type (Go-tone Whisker against Nogo-tone Whisker, p 0.0547), so that variant is also partial.

fig3c-delay-modulation-wm2-alm¶

In the last 200 ms of the delay of quiet Hit trials, more wM2 than ALM neurons are up-modulated relative to baseline (16.0% against 14.2%, p = 0.0499) and fewer are down-modulated (14.3% against 17.0%, p = 0.0062), by chi-squared tests.

As code, Modulation.m: counts in 0.8 to 1.0 s against -0.2 to 0 s of the same trials (bins 181:200 and 81:100), SI = 2(AUC - 0.5), 200 label permutations. Three permutation seeds; the code's mean absolute deviation as a variant.

In [22]:
W_DELAY, W_PRE = np.arange(180, 200), np.arange(80, 100)


def modulation(area, rule, rng):
    si, p = [], []
    for s, cols in g.area_sessions(S, area):
        sel = g.trial_mask(s, 1, True) & g.quiet_mask(s, rule)
        if sel.sum() == 0:
            continue
        X = s["c10"][sel][:, :, cols].astype(float)
        w_, b_ = X[:, W_DELAY].sum(axis=1), X[:, W_PRE].sum(axis=1)
        for j in range(len(cols)):
            r = g.roc_test(w_[:, j], b_[:, j], 200, rng)
            si.append(r[0])
            p.append(r[1])
    return np.array(si), np.array(p)


rows = []
for rule in ("median", "mean"):
    for seed in (5, 6, 7):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        R = {a: modulation(a, rule, rng) for a in ("wM2", "ALM")}
        for kind, sign in (("up", 1), ("down", -1)):
            k = {a: (np.sign(R[a][0]) == sign) & (R[a][1] < 0.05) for a in R}
            tab = [[k["wM2"].sum(), (~k["wM2"]).sum()], [k["ALM"].sum(), (~k["ALM"]).sum()]]
            rows.append({"MAD": rule, "seed": seed, "kind": kind, "wM2 %": 100 * k["wM2"].mean(), "ALM %": 100 * k["ALM"].mean(),
                         "wM2 n": len(k["wM2"]), "ALM n": len(k["ALM"]),
                         "chi2 p": stats.chi2_contingency(tab, correction=False).pvalue})
mod = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(mod.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("\nPaper: up 16.0 (wM2) and 14.2 (ALM), p 0.0499; down 14.3 and 17.0, p 0.0062. Tolerances 10%.")

Result: partially reproduced. Under the Methods' quiet rule both directions hold and both tests are significant for every seed (up: wM2 13.6 to 13.8% against ALM 11.6 to 11.8%, p 0.020 to 0.037; down: 10.9 to 11.1% against 13.6 to 14.0%, p 0.0006 to 0.0046), but all four fractions are below tolerance. With the code's mean absolute deviation, which keeps more trials, the fractions are the paper's (up 16.0 to 16.3% against 14.3%, down 14.0 to 14.3% against 17.0%), and the up-modulation test gives p 0.047 to 0.077 depending on the seed, against the paper's 0.0499.

fig3d-wm2-infragranular-delay¶

During the late delay of Go-tone Whisker trials, wM2 infragranular neurons change their firing more than supragranular neurons (1.2 +/- 0.1 Hz against 0.03 +/- 0.10 Hz, p = 1.7 x 10^-7, two-sample t-test), while no layer difference is detected in A1, wS2 or ALM.

Result: partially reproduced. In wM2 infragranular neurons change by 0.955 +/- 0.119 Hz and supragranular by -0.055 +/- 0.093 Hz (t-test p 1.6e-06; wM2 has no layer 4 units); the supragranular value is within tolerance, the infragranular one below it (1.1 to 1.3). No layer pair differs in A1, wS2 or ALM (smallest p 0.21). With the code's mean absolute deviation the wM2 values are 1.128 and -0.003 Hz (p 2.0e-07), within tolerance. The criterion's partial case does not cover this result (the wM2 test holds and no other pair is significant, but one value is out of tolerance); it is recorded as partial since the effect is there and one number misses.

cluster-label-link¶

The paper's cluster labels (Zenodo, processed_data/Data_Clustering.mat) can be matched to the dataset's units by the code's global unit index.

The global index is rebuilt as psth_10ms.m builds it (helper global_ids). The link holds when every labelled neuron maps to a unit of the dataset whose probe area, CCF label and layer are the ones the label file gives, and the unit is one of the 10,294 analysed here.

In [24]:
t0 = time.time()
CL = g.cluster_labels()
print(f"read {len(CL['cluster'])} cluster labels in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s; clusters {CL['cluster'].min()} to {CL['cluster'].max()}")
GID = g.global_ids(S)
print("global indices built:", len(GID), "; units in the dataset:", sum(len(s["units"]["location"]) for s in S))
match = {"mapped": 0, "area": 0, "ccf": 0, "layer": 0, "analysed": 0}
unit_cluster = {}
for gi, cl, ar, cc, la in zip(CL["global_id"], CL["cluster"], CL["area"], CL["ccf"], CL["layer"]):
    if gi not in GID:
        continue
    i, u = GID[gi]
    U = S[i]["units"]
    match["mapped"] += 1
    match["area"] += U["location"][u] == ar
    match["ccf"] += U["ccf_location"][u] == cc
    match["layer"] += U["allenccf_area_layer"][u] == la
    match["analysed"] += U["area"][u] == ar
    unit_cluster[(i, u)] = cl
n = len(CL["cluster"])
print({k: f"{v} of {n}" for k, v in match.items()})
print("Distinct dataset units matched:", len(unit_cluster))

fig4b-named-clusters¶

Some clusters represent sensory responses (cluster 1, fast auditory response, mostly A1 neurons; cluster 29, fast whisker response, mostly wS1 and wS2), clusters 11 and 25 fire during the delay only on Go-tone trials and consist mainly of wM2 and ALM neurons, and cluster 4 decreases its firing during the Go-tone delay and is spread over the five areas.

PSTHs as fig3b-delay-and-response-psth (quiet correct trials, baseline -1 to 0 s). The response of clusters 1 and 29 is shown for each correct trial type that has the stimulus.

In [25]:
def cluster_of(s_index, area):
    s = S[s_index]
    rows_ = s["keep"][g.area_columns(s, area)]
    return np.array([unit_cluster.get((s_index, int(u)), 0) for u in rows_])


comp = []
for a in g.AREAS:
    for i in range(len(S)):
        for c_ in cluster_of(i, a):
            comp.append((c_, a))
comp = pd.DataFrame(comp, columns=["cluster", "area"])
share = pd.crosstab(comp.cluster, comp.area, normalize="index")[g.AREAS] * 100
counts = pd.crosstab(comp.cluster, comp.area)[g.AREAS]
print("Neurons per cluster and area (%), clusters 1, 4, 11, 25, 29:")
print(pd.concat([counts.loc[[1, 4, 11, 25, 29]].sum(axis=1).rename("n"), share.loc[[1, 4, 11, 25, 29]].round(1)], axis=1).to_string())


def cluster_window(cl, masks, window):
    out = [[] for _ in masks]
    for a in g.AREAS:
        for i, s in enumerate(S):
            cols = g.area_columns(s, a)
            if len(cols) == 0:
                continue
            sel_cols = cols[cluster_of(i, a) == cl]
            if len(sel_cols) == 0:
                continue
            q = g.quiet_mask(s)
            for k, m in enumerate(masks):
                mm = m(s) & q
                if mm.sum() == 0:
                    continue
                x = s["c10"][mm][:, :, sel_cols].mean(axis=0) / g.W10
                out[k].append(x[g.bin_index(*window)].mean(axis=0) - x[g.bin_index(-1, 0)].mean(axis=0))
    return [np.concatenate(o) for o in out]


tone_types = [lambda s, t_=t_: g.correct_mask(s, t_) for t_ in (1, 2, 3, 4)]
whisk_types = [lambda s, t_=t_: g.correct_mask(s, t_) for t_ in (1, 3, 5)]
r1 = cluster_window(1, tone_types, (0.01, 0.03))
r29 = cluster_window(29, whisk_types, (1.01, 1.03))
print("\nCluster 1, mean change 0 to 30 ms (Hz), trial types 1-4:", [round(x.mean(), 2) for x in r1])
print("Cluster 29, mean change 1.00 to 1.03 s (Hz), trial types 1, 3, 5:", [round(x.mean(), 2) for x in r29])
for cl in (11, 25, 4):
    h_, n_ = cluster_window(cl, [lambda s: g.correct_mask(s, 1), lambda s: g.correct_mask(s, 3)], (0.8, 1.0))
    print(f"Cluster {cl}, 0.8 to 1.0 s: Hit {h_.mean():.2f} Hz, Nogo-tone Whisker CR {n_.mean():.2f} Hz "
          f"(neurons {len(h_)}, {len(n_)})")


def mostly(cl, group):
    sh = share.loc[cl]
    a_ = sh[list(group)].sum() > 50
    b_ = set(sh.sort_values(ascending=False).index[:len(group)]) == set(group)
    return a_, b_


for cl, group in ((1, ("A1",)), (29, ("wS1", "wS2")), (11, ("wM2", "ALM")), (25, ("wM2", "ALM"))):
    a_, b_ = mostly(cl, group)
    print(f"Cluster {cl} mostly {group}: reading (a) more than half: {a_}; reading (b) largest share: {b_}")
print("Cluster 4, share in each area (%):", share.loc[4].round(1).to_dict(), "; at least 5% in each:", bool((share.loc[4] >= 5).all()))

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). Parts (2) to (4) hold under both readings of "mostly": cluster 29 is 45.2% wS1 and 41.5% wS2 with a whisker response of 21.7 to 21.9 Hz; clusters 11 and 25 are 90.4% and 83.1% wM2 and ALM and fire more in Hit than in Nogo CR trials over the late delay (11.54 against -0.79 Hz, 3.56 against -0.29 Hz); cluster 4 fires less in Hit (-1.60 against 0.05 Hz) and has 7.1 to 31.9% of its neurons in each area. Cluster 1 has a fast auditory response (13.0 to 17.3 Hz) and its largest share in A1 (30.5%), but not more than half: reading (b) gives reproduced and reading (a) partially reproduced. The criterion blocks the claim when the readings differ.

fig5a-single-neuron-context¶

Comparing Hit with Nogo-tone Whisker correct rejection trials in the last 200 ms of the delay, wM2 and ALM have the highest proportions of context-modulated neurons (wM2, 20% increase firing by 8 Hz on average, 14% decrease by 3 Hz; ALM, 17% increase by 8 Hz, 16% decrease by 3 Hz), and wM2 has the largest proportion of Go-tone excited neurons.

As code, Roc_hit_cr3.m: counts in bins 181:200 (0.8 to 1.0 s) of quiet Hit against quiet Nogo-tone Whisker CR trials, SI and 200-permutation p; the change is the Hit minus CR mean rate.

rows = []
for rule in ("median", "mean"):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(8)
    for a in g.AREAS:
        si, p, d = [], [], []
        for s, cols in g.area_sessions(S, a):
            q = g.quiet_mask(s, rule)
            m1, m2 = g.trial_mask(s, 1, True) & q, g.trial_mask(s, 3, False) & q
            if m1.sum() == 0 or m2.sum() == 0:
                continue
            x = s["c10"][m1][:, W_DELAY][:, :, cols].sum(axis=1).astype(float)
            y = s["c10"][m2][:, W_DELAY][:, :, cols].sum(axis=1).astype(float)
            for j in range(len(cols)):
                r = g.roc_test(x[:, j], y[:, j], 200, rng)
                si.append(r[0])
                p.append(r[1])
            d.append(x.mean(axis=0) / 0.2 - y.mean(axis=0) / 0.2)
        si, p, d = np.array(si), np.array(p), np.concatenate(d)
        up, dn = (si > 0) & (p < 0.05), (si < 0) & (p < 0.05)
        rows.append({"MAD": rule, "area": a, "neurons": len(si), "up %": 100 * up.mean(), "up mean Hz": d[up].mean(),
                     "down %": 100 * dn.mean(), "down mean Hz": d[dn].mean(), "modulated %": 100 * (up | dn).mean()})
ctx = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(ctx.round(2).to_string(index=False))

         ("ALM", "up %"): (17, 1.7), ("ALM", "up mean Hz"): (8, 0.8), ("ALM", "down %"): (16, 1.6), ("ALM", "down mean Hz"): (-3, 0.5)}
for rule in ("median", "mean"):

    within = {f"{a} {k}": bool(abs(sub.loc[a, k] - v) <= tol) for (a, k), (v, tol) in exp5a.items()}
    print(f"\n{rule}: within tolerance {sum(within.values())} of 8: {within}")

fig6a-pca-delay-states¶

In the first two PCs, A1, wS1 and wS2 activity returns near its start by the end of the delay, while in correct Go-tone trials wM2 and ALM settle within about 200 ms into a state far from the origin, reached with and without the whisker stimulus; Nogo correct rejections return to baseline and Miss trials fail to reach the Go-tone state. PC1 explains 11% (A1, wS1, wS2), 17% (wM2) and 14% (ALM) of variance, PC2 6% (A1, wS1, wS2) and 8% (wM2, ALM).

As code, Ghaderi2025_Figure6_a_pca.m: per area all neurons, mean over quiet completed trials of Hit, Nogo-tone Whisker CR, Go-tone No-Whisker CR and Miss in 50 ms bins, baseline (-1 to 0 s) subtracted, the four conditions concatenated (240 time points), neurons with no range (or no trials of a condition) dropped, each divided by its range; PCA over time points.

CONDS6 = [("Hit", 1, True), ("Nogo CR", 3, False), ("Go NoW CR", 2, False), ("Miss", 1, False)]


def pca_area(area, rule, fit_on=None):
    blocks = []
    for s, cols in g.area_sessions(S, area):
        q = g.quiet_mask(s, rule)
        M = []
        for _, t_, l_ in CONDS6:
            m = g.trial_mask(s, t_, l_) & q
            if m.sum():
                x = s["c10"][m][:, :, cols].astype(float).reshape(m.sum(), 60, 5, len(cols)).sum(axis=2).mean(axis=0)
            else:
                x = np.full((60, len(cols)), np.nan)
            M.append(x - x[:20].mean(axis=0))
        blocks.append(np.concatenate(M, axis=0))
    X = np.concatenate(blocks, axis=1).T
    rng_ = X.max(axis=1) - X.min(axis=1)
    ok = np.isfinite(rng_) & (rng_ > 0)
    X = (X[ok] / rng_[ok, None]).T
    fit = X if fit_on is None else X[np.concatenate([np.arange(i * 60, (i + 1) * 60) for i in fit_on])]
    mu = fit.mean(axis=0)
    _, sv, Vt = np.linalg.svd(fit - mu, full_matrices=False)
    ev = 100 * sv ** 2 / (sv ** 2).sum()
    P = (X - X.mean(axis=0)) @ Vt[:2].T if fit_on is None else (X - mu) @ Vt[:2].T
    dist = []
    for i in range(4):
        seg = P[i * 60:(i + 1) * 60]
        dist.append(np.linalg.norm(seg[36:40].mean(axis=0) - seg[:20].mean(axis=0)))
    hitseg = P[:60]
    dh = np.linalg.norm(hitseg - hitseg[:20].mean(axis=0), axis=1)
    return {"area": area, "neurons kept": int(ok.sum()), "neurons": len(ok), "PC1 %": ev[0], "PC2 %": ev[1],
            **{f"dist {c[0]}": d_ for c, d_ in zip(CONDS6, dist)}, "Hit dist at 1.0 / max 0-1 s": dh[39] / dh[20:40].max()}, P


exp6 = {"A1": (11, 6), "wS1": (11, 6), "wS2": (11, 6), "wM2": (17, 8), "ALM": (14, 8)}
pca_rows, projections = [], {}
for variant, rule, fit_on in (("main", "median", None), ("code MAD (mean)", "mean", None), ("legend: fit on Hit and Nogo CR", "median", (0, 1))):
    for a in g.AREAS:
        r, P_ = pca_area(a, rule, fit_on)
        r["variant"] = variant
        r["PC1 within"] = abs(r["PC1 %"] - exp6[a][0]) <= 0.1 * exp6[a][0]
        r["PC2 within"] = abs(r["PC2 %"] - exp6[a][1]) <= 0.1 * exp6[a][1]
        if a in ("wM2", "ALM"):
            r["geometry"] = min(r["dist Hit"], r["dist Go NoW CR"]) > max(r["dist Nogo CR"], r["dist Miss"])
        else:
            r["geometry"] = r["Hit dist at 1.0 / max 0-1 s"] < 0.5
        pca_rows.append(r)
        if variant == "main":
            projections[a] = P_
pca_tab = pd.DataFrame(pca_rows)
print(pca_tab.round(3).to_string(index=False))

fig6b-context-coding-direction¶

Projected on a context coding direction, late-delay activity in wM2 and ALM is high in Hit trials and significantly lower in Nogo-tone, Go-tone No-Whisker and Miss trials.

As the criterion: per area-session with at least 5 neurons, CD context from a random 20% of quiet Hit and of quiet Nogo CR trials (Methods; 30% in the code, a variant), the mean over bins labelled 0.8 to 1.0 s of the difference of mean count vectors, unit length (Gram-Schmidt with the later directions leaves it unchanged); held-out Hit and Nogo CR trials and all Go-tone No-Whisker CR and Miss trials projected; per session the mean projection over 0.8 to 1.0 s; Wilcoxon, p times 3.

In [29]:
WCTX = g.bin_index(0.8, 1.0)


def cd_context(frac, rule, rng):
    rows = []
    for a in g.AREAS:
        for s, cols in g.area_sessions(S, a, 5):
            q = g.quiet_mask(s, rule)
            X = s["c10"][:, :, cols].astype(float)
            ids = {name: np.flatnonzero(g.trial_mask(s, t_, l_) & q) for name, t_, l_ in CONDS6}
            h_tr, h_te = g.split_train(ids["Hit"], frac, rng)
            c_tr, c_te = g.split_train(ids["Nogo CR"], frac, rng)
            if len(h_tr) == 0 or len(c_tr) == 0:
                rows.append({"area": a, "session": s["session"], "dropped": True})
                continue
            cd = X[h_tr][:, WCTX].mean(axis=(0, 1)) - X[c_tr][:, WCTX].mean(axis=(0, 1))
            cd /= np.linalg.norm(cd)
            pr = lambda t: (X[t][:, WCTX] @ cd).mean() if len(t) else np.nan
            rows.append({"area": a, "session": s["session"], "dropped": False, "Hit": pr(h_te), "Nogo CR": pr(c_te),
                         "Go NoW CR": pr(ids["Go NoW CR"]), "Miss": pr(ids["Miss"])})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def hit_vs(df, others, factor=3):
    out = []
    for a in g.AREAS:
        sub = df[(df.area == a) & ~df.dropped]
        for o in others:
            ok = sub["Hit"].notna() & sub[o].notna()
            p_ = stats.wilcoxon(sub.loc[ok, "Hit"], sub.loc[ok, o]).pvalue
            out.append({"area": a, "vs": o, "sessions": int(ok.sum()), "Hit": sub.loc[ok, "Hit"].mean(),
                        "other": sub.loc[ok, o].mean(), "diff": (sub.loc[ok, "Hit"] - sub.loc[ok, o]).mean(),
                        "p x3": min(1.0, factor * p_)})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


for frac, rule, seed in ((0.2, "median", 9), (0.3, "median", 9), (0.2, "mean", 9), (0.2, "median", 10)):
    df = cd_context(frac, rule, np.random.default_rng(seed))
    res = hit_vs(df, ["Nogo CR", "Go NoW CR", "Miss"])
    res["holds"] = (res["diff"] > 0) & (res["p x3"] < 0.05)
    print(f"Training fraction {frac}, MAD {rule}, seed {seed}; area-sessions dropped (no training trials): {int(df.dropped.sum())}")
    print(res.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print("  wM2 and ALM, comparisons holding:", int(res[res.area.isin(["wM2", "ALM"])].holds.sum()), "of 6\n")

fig6c-temporal-correlation¶

In wM2 and ALM the Go-tone induces a long-lasting increase in correlated population activity during the delay in Hit and Go-tone No-Whisker trials, absent in Nogo-tone and Miss trials, while in A1, wS1 and wS2 the cue evokes only a brief increase.

As the criterion (code, Temporal_corrrelation_10ms.m and Ghaderi2025_Figure6_c_temporalCorrelation.m).

off = np.ones((100, 100)) - np.eye(100)
off[off == 0] = np.nan
rows, maps = [], {}
for a in g.AREAS:
    for s, cols in g.area_sessions(S, a, 5):
        q = g.quiet_mask(s)
        row = {"area": a, "session": s["session"]}
        for name, t_, l_ in CONDS6:
            m = g.trial_mask(s, t_, l_) & q
            if m.sum() == 0:
                row[name] = np.nan
                continue
            R = g.temporal_correlation(s["c10"][m][:, :, cols])
            R = R - np.nanmean(R[:100, :100] * off)
            row[name] = np.nanmean(R[99:200, 99:200])
            maps.setdefault((a, name), []).append(R)
        rows.append(row)

As the criterion (code, psth_5ms.m and Ghaderi2025_Figure7_b_DeltaFR.m). Bins are labelled by their right edge, as in the code.

fig7c-no-whisker-cd-change¶

Activity projected on a whisker coding direction, defined from the first 30 ms of No-tone Whisker responses, shows no significant difference between Go-tone and Nogo-tone contexts.

As the criterion (code, Coding_direction_5ms.m and Ghaderi2025_Figure7_c_StimCD.m), with 30% training trials (code). The 5 ms counts kept by the helper start at 0.95 s, so the -1 to 0 s baseline of the whisker direction and the 0.8 to 1.0 s window of the context direction are taken from the 10 ms counts divided by 2 (the mean count per 5 ms); the context window is then [0.79, 1.0) in place of [0.795, 1.0). The projection is the 5 ms bin labelled 1.030 s.

In [33]:
B10 = g.bin_index(-1.0, 0.0)
I_WHISK = np.arange(9, 16)      # 5 ms bins labelled 1.000 to 1.030 s
I_30 = 15                       # bin labelled 1.030 s
GROUPS8 = [("Go lick", 1, True), ("Go no lick", 1, False), ("Nogo lick", 3, True), ("Nogo no lick", 3, False),
           ("No-tone lick", 5, True), ("No-tone no lick", 5, False)]


def coding_directions_5ms(frac, rule, rng):
    rows7, rows8 = [], []
    for a in g.AREAS:
        for s, cols in g.area_sessions(S, a, 5):
            q = g.quiet_mask(s, rule)
            X10 = s["c10"][:, :, cols].astype(float)
            X5 = s["c5"][:, :, cols].astype(float)
            hit = np.flatnonzero(g.trial_mask(s, 1, True) & q)
            cr = np.flatnonzero(g.trial_mask(s, 3, False) & q)
            wt = np.flatnonzero(g.trial_mask(s, 5, False) & q)
            h_tr, h_te = g.split_train(hit, frac, rng)
            c_tr, c_te = g.split_train(cr, frac, rng)
            w_tr, w_te = g.split_train(wt, frac, rng)
            if min(len(h_tr), len(c_tr), len(w_tr)) == 0:
                continue
            cdc = (X10[h_tr][:, WCTX].mean(axis=(0, 1)) - X10[c_tr][:, WCTX].mean(axis=(0, 1))) / 2
            cdc /= np.linalg.norm(cdc)
            cdw = X5[w_tr][:, I_WHISK].mean(axis=(0, 1)) - X10[w_tr][:, B10].mean(axis=(0, 1)) / 2
            cdw /= np.linalg.norm(cdw)
            cdw = cdw - (cdw @ cdc) * cdc
            cdw /= np.linalg.norm(cdw)
            pr = lambda t, cd: (X5[t][:, I_30] @ cd).mean() if len(t) else np.nan
            rows7.append({"area": a, "session": s["session"], "Hit": pr(h_te, cdw), "Nogo CR": pr(c_te, cdw)})
            train = set(h_tr) | set(c_tr)
            row = {"area": a, "session": s["session"]}
            for name, t_, l_ in GROUPS8:
                ids = np.array([i for i in np.flatnonzero(g.trial_mask(s, t_, l_) & q) if i not in train], int)
                row[name] = pr(ids, cdc)
            rows8.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows7), pd.DataFrame(rows8)


cd7, cd8 = {}, {}
for key, (frac, rule, seed) in {"main": (0.3, "median", 11), "20% training": (0.2, "median", 11),
                                "code MAD (mean)": (0.3, "mean", 11), "seed 12": (0.3, "median", 12)}.items():
    cd7[key], cd8[key] = coding_directions_5ms(frac, rule, np.random.default_rng(seed))
for key, df in cd7.items():

    print(f"Whisker CD at 30 ms, {key}:")
    print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(4).to_string(index=False))

Result: reproduced. The Kruskal-Wallis test finds no difference between Hit and Nogo CR projections on the whisker direction in any area (p 0.31 to 0.97), as the claim of absence requires, and the variants agree (smallest p 0.19). The paired Wilcoxon test, not the paper's, gives p 0.096 in wS2 (Hit higher by 0.044) and p above 0.15 elsewhere; in the variants it falls below 0.05 in wS2 (20% training, code's MAD) and A1 (code's MAD).

Result: partially reproduced. In wM2 the six groups differ (Kruskal-Wallis p 0.0048) and Go-tone lick trials project above Go-tone no-lick trials (LSD p 0.0041), but Nogo-tone lick (false alarm) trials are not significantly above Nogo-tone no-lick trials (p 0.28): wM2 holds for one of the two contexts. A1, wS1 and wS2 show no significant lick against no-lick comparison (all p 0.40 or more). ALM gives Kruskal-Wallis p below 0.0001, Go-tone p 0.0008 and Nogo-tone p 0.028. The variants agree that the Nogo-tone comparison in wM2 is not significant (p 0.08 to 0.36). The legend of Supplementary Fig. 17 gives wM2's Nogo-tone result as "Nogo-tone Lick vs No tone no lick trials" (p 0.04); that pair, not the criterion's, gives p 0.22 in wM2 (variants 0.09 to 0.37), also not significant. Whether the criterion's pair is the paper's is asked of a reader.

fig8b-lick-coding-direction¶

At 30 ms after the whisker stimulus, activity along a lick coding direction defined from spontaneous licking separates lick from no-lick trials in wM2 for Go-tone, Nogo-tone (false alarm) and No-tone trials, in ALM only for correct trials, and not in A1, wS1 or wS2.

As the criterion (code, Coding_direction_SpontLick.m and Ghaderi2025_Figure8_b_SpontLick_CD_LickvsNolick.m). The detected lick times and the lick mask come from data_helpers/Lick_times.mat on the Zenodo record, which the dandiset does not hold; the jaw trace and video timestamps the rule also needs are taken from the dandiset, and the file's copies are checked against them. Spontaneous licks: outside 0 to 6 s of every trial start, in a lick-mask bout longer than 0.5 s, and with the mean jaw trace over 0 to 0.1 s after the lick above 3 times its mean over -1 to 0 s; area-sessions (at least 5 neurons) with fewer than 2 such licks are dropped. CD lick per area-session: the mean over licks of each neuron's mean 5 ms count over 0.2 to 0.5 s after the lick minus that over -1 to -0.5 s, unit length. Quiet completed trials are projected (5 ms bin labelled 1.030 s) and averaged per group; a group with fewer than 2 trials in a session is left out (code, min_num_trials = 2). Kruskal-Wallis over the six groups, then Fisher LSD. No trial is used to train CD lick, so all trials are projected.

# What the dataset holds of licking: the contents of each session's behaviour module (verifier's
# question; the lick times come from Lick_times.mat because no detected lick times are here).
def behaviour_module(asset):
    path, _, aid = asset
    f = g.open_nwb(aid)
    pb = f["processing/behavior"]
    out = {"session": path.split("/")[-1][:33],
           "BehavioralEvents": ", ".join(sorted(pb["BehavioralEvents"].keys())) if "BehavioralEvents" in pb else "",
           "BehavioralTimeSeries": ", ".join(sorted(pb["BehavioralTimeSeries"].keys())) if "BehavioralTimeSeries" in pb else ""}
    f.close()
    return out


with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    bmod = pd.DataFrame(list(ex.map(behaviour_module, g.ephys_assets())))
print("Contents of processing/behavior over the", len(bmod), "sessions (distinct combinations, with session counts):")
print(bmod.groupby(["BehavioralEvents", "BehavioralTimeSeries"]).size().reset_index(name="sessions").to_string(index=False))

t0 = time.time()
LT, n_lick_entries, lick_mismatch = g.lick_times()
print(f"Lick_times.mat: {n_lick_entries} probe entries for {len(LT)} sessions, read in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s; "
      f"entries of one session that differ: {lick_mismatch}")
print("sessions of the dataset without an entry:", [s["session"] for s in S if s["session"] not in LT])


def spont_session(s):
    r = LT[s["session"]]
    ts, jaw = g.jaw_trace(s["path"])
    same = len(ts) == len(r["video_ts"]) and np.array_equal(ts, r["video_ts"])
    jaw_diff = float(np.nanmax(np.abs(jaw - r["jaw"]))) if same else np.nan
    same = same and bool(np.array_equal(np.isnan(jaw), np.isnan(r["jaw"])))
    sp, cnt = g.spontaneous_licks(r["lick_time"], r["lick_mask"], ts, jaw, s["trials"]["start_time"])
    return {"session": s["session"], "licks in file": len(r["lick_time"]), **cnt, "spontaneous": len(sp),
            "file timestamps and NaNs = dataset's": same, "largest jaw difference": jaw_diff, "mask frames = video frames": len(r["lick_mask"]) == len(ts)}, sp


with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    out = list(ex.map(spont_session, S))
SPONT = {r["session"]: sp for r, sp in out}
spont_tab = pd.DataFrame([r for r, _ in out])

      "; all jaw traces and timestamps equal to the dataset's:", bool(spont_tab["file timestamps and NaNs = dataset's"].all()),
      "; largest jaw difference over sessions:", spont_tab["largest jaw difference"].max())

GROUPS8B = [("Go lick", 1, True), ("Nogo lick", 3, True), ("No-tone lick", 5, True),
            ("Go no lick", 1, False), ("Nogo no lick", 3, False), ("No-tone no lick", 5, False)]
W_AFTER, W_BEFORE = (0.2, 0.5), (-1.0, -0.5)     # code, params.Win_lick and params.Win_nolick
W_S18 = g.bin_index(1.2, 1.4)                     # Supplementary Fig. 18 window, from the 10 ms counts


def lick_cd_session(s):
    """CD lick of each area of a session (unit length is applied later)."""
    sp = SPONT[s["session"]]
    cols = {a: g.area_columns(s, a) for a in g.AREAS}
    cols = {a: c for a, c in cols.items() if len(c) >= 5}
    if not cols or len(sp) < 2:
        return s["session"], {}
    allc = np.concatenate(list(cols.values()))
    C = g.event_counts(s["path"], s["keep"][allc], sp, (W_AFTER, W_BEFORE))
    pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(allc)}
    # mean 5 ms count per bin: 60 bins in 0.2 to 0.5 s, 100 in -1 to -0.5 s
    return s["session"], {a: C[0][:, [pos[c] for c in cl]].mean(axis=0) / 60 - C[1][:, [pos[c] for c in cl]].mean(axis=0) / 100
                          for a, cl in cols.items()}


t0 = time.time()
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    CDL = dict(ex.map(lick_cd_session, S))
print(f"spike counts around spontaneous licks: {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")


def lick_projections(rule, min_trials=2):
    rows, dropped = [], []
    for a in g.AREAS:
        for s, cols in g.area_sessions(S, a, 5):
            cd = CDL[s["session"]].get(a)
            if cd is None or np.linalg.norm(cd) == 0:
                dropped.append((a, s["session"]))
                continue
            cd = cd / np.linalg.norm(cd)
            q = g.quiet_mask(s, rule)
            p30 = s["c5"][:, I_30, cols].astype(float) @ cd
            plate = (s["c10"][:, W_S18][:, :, cols].astype(float) @ cd).mean(axis=1) / 2   # 10 ms counts halved
            row = {"area": a, "session": s["session"], "subject": s["subject"], "spontaneous licks": len(SPONT[s["session"]])}
            for name, t_, l_ in GROUPS8B:
                m = g.trial_mask(s, t_, l_) & q
                row[name] = p30[m].mean() if m.sum() >= min_trials else np.nan
                row[name + " (1.2-1.4 s)"] = plate[m].mean() if m.sum() >= min_trials else np.nan
                row["n " + name] = int(m.sum())
            rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), dropped


def lick_tests(df, suffix=""):
    rows = []
    for a in g.AREAS:
        sub = df[df.area == a]
        H, p_, comps = g.kruskal_lsd([sub[name + suffix] for name, *_ in GROUPS8B])
        row = {"area": a, "sessions": len(sub), "KW H": H, "KW p": p_}
        for i, ctx in enumerate(("Go", "Nogo", "No-tone")):
            for j, ctx2 in zip(range(3, 6), ("Go", "Nogo", "No-tone")):
                d, pp = comps[(i, j)]
                row[f"{ctx} lick vs {ctx2} no lick p"] = pp
                row[f"{ctx} lick vs {ctx2} no lick sign"] = "+" if d > 0 else "-"
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


LP, lick_tab = {}, {}
for rule in ("median", "mean"):
    LP[rule], dropped8b = lick_projections(rule)
    lick_tab[rule] = lick_tests(LP[rule])
    print(f"\nQuiet rule MAD = {rule}; area-sessions dropped for fewer than 2 spontaneous licks: {len(dropped8b)}")
    print("Mean projection at 1.030 s by group:")
    print(LP[rule].groupby("area")[[n for n, *_ in GROUPS8B]].mean().loc[g.AREAS].round(3).to_string())
    print("Range of the per-session group means:", round(float(np.nanmin(LP[rule][[n for n, *_ in GROUPS8B]].values)), 3),
          "to", round(float(np.nanmax(LP[rule][[n for n, *_ in GROUPS8B]].values)), 3))
    print(lick_tab[rule].round(4).T.to_string())


def within(tab, area, ctx):
    r = tab.set_index("area").loc[area]
    return r[f"{ctx} lick vs {ctx} no lick p"] < 0.05 and r[f"{ctx} lick vs {ctx} no lick sign"] == "+"


for rule in ("median", "mean"):
    t_ = lick_tab[rule]
    wm2 = [within(t_, "wM2", c) for c in ("Go", "Nogo", "No-tone")]
    alm = (within(t_, "ALM", "Go"), within(t_, "ALM", "Nogo"))
    sens = {a: [c for c in ("Go", "Nogo", "No-tone")
                if t_.set_index("area").loc[a, f"{c} lick vs {c} no lick p"] < 0.05] for a in ("A1", "wS1", "wS2")}
    sens_all = {a: int(sum(t_.set_index("area").loc[a, f"{c} lick vs {c2} no lick p"] < 0.05
                           for c in ("Go", "Nogo", "No-tone") for c2 in ("Go", "Nogo", "No-tone"))) for a in ("A1", "wS1", "wS2")}
    print(f"\nMAD = {rule}: wM2 KW p < 0.05: {bool(t_.set_index('area').loc['wM2', 'KW p'] < 0.05)}; "
          f"wM2 lick above no lick (Go, Nogo, No-tone): {wm2}; ALM Go significant {alm[0]}, Nogo significant {alm[1]}; "
          f"A1, wS1, wS2 contexts with a significant lick vs no lick comparison: {sens}; "
          f"of all 9 lick vs no-lick pairs: {sens_all}")
print("\nwM2 sessions per group (median MAD):", LP["median"][LP["median"].area == "wM2"][[n for n, *_ in GROUPS8B]].notna().sum().to_dict())
print("wM2 and ALM area-sessions per mouse:", LP["median"][LP["median"].area.isin(["wM2", "ALM"])].groupby(["area", "subject"]).size().to_dict())

Result: reproduced. Of the 35 sessions 23 have at least 2 spontaneous licks (the lick file's jaw trace and timestamps equal the dataset's), which leaves 12 wM2, 10 ALM, 9 A1, 16 wS1 and 16 wS2 area-sessions (the paper: 10 to 12 for wM2). In wM2 the six groups differ (Kruskal-Wallis p 0.0036) and each context's lick group is above its own no-lick group (LSD p 0.044 Go-tone, 0.0064 Nogo-tone, 0.015 No-tone; against the three no-lick groups p 0.0064 to 0.044, the paper 0.002 to 0.04). In ALM Go-tone lick trials are above Go-tone no-lick trials (p 0.042) and Nogo-tone lick trials are not (p 0.45), although ALM's Kruskal-Wallis test is not significant (p 0.155). A1, wS1 and wS2 have no significant lick against no-lick comparison (p 0.30 or more). The code's quiet rule gives the same pattern (wM2 Kruskal-Wallis p 0.0011; ALM Go-tone p 0.033, Nogo-tone p 0.30).

figs18-later-lick-coding¶

Later, at 0.2 to 0.4 s after the whisker stimulus, the lick coding direction separates lick from no-lick trials in ALM, wM2, wS2 and wS1, with the effect largest in ALM and ranked in that order.

The projections of fig8b-lick-coding-direction averaged over 1.2 to 1.4 s (code, Ghaderi2025_Sup_Figure18_SpontLick_CD_LickvsNolick_200mswindow.m), with the same Kruskal-Wallis and LSD tests. The 5 ms counts are kept only up to 1.10 s, so this window is taken from the 10 ms counts halved (bins labelled 1.20 to 1.40 s, [1.19, 1.40) in place of [1.195, 1.40)); a projection is linear, so this changes only the window edge. Effect size readings (criterion): (a) Cohen's d of the session-group means of the three lick groups against the three no-lick groups, (b) the Kruskal-Wallis statistic.

for rule in ("median", "mean"):
    df = LP[rule]
    t18 = lick_tests(df, " (1.2-1.4 s)")
    rows = []
    for a in g.AREAS:
        sub = df[df.area == a]
        lk = np.concatenate([sub[n + " (1.2-1.4 s)"].dropna().values for n, _, l in GROUPS8B if l])
        nl = np.concatenate([sub[n + " (1.2-1.4 s)"].dropna().values for n, _, l in GROUPS8B if not l])
        sp = np.sqrt(((len(lk) - 1) * lk.var(ddof=1) + (len(nl) - 1) * nl.var(ddof=1)) / (len(lk) + len(nl) - 2))
        r = t18.set_index("area").loc[a]
        n_sig_up = int(sum((r[f"{c} lick vs {c2} no lick p"] < 0.05) and r[f"{c} lick vs {c2} no lick sign"] == "+"
                           for c in ("Go", "Nogo", "No-tone") for c2 in ("Go", "Nogo", "No-tone")))
        rows.append({"area": a, "sessions": len(sub), "mean lick": lk.mean(), "mean no lick": nl.mean(),
                     "(a) Cohen's d": (lk.mean() - nl.mean()) / sp, "(b) KW H": r["KW H"], "KW p": r["KW p"],
                     "lick > no lick pairs significant (of 9)": n_sig_up,
                     "within-context significant (Go, Nogo, No-tone)": [within(t18, a, c) for c in ("Go", "Nogo", "No-tone")]})
    eff = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    print(f"Quiet rule MAD = {rule}, 1.2 to 1.4 s:")
    print(eff.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    eff["difference (not a criterion reading)"] = eff["mean lick"] - eff["mean no lick"]
    for col in ("(a) Cohen's d", "(b) KW H", "difference (not a criterion reading)"):
        print(f"  ranking by {col}: {eff.sort_values(col, ascending=False).area.tolist()}")
    four = eff.set_index("area").loc[["ALM", "wM2", "wS2", "wS1"]]
    print("  ALM, wM2, wS2 and wS1 each KW p < 0.05 with a lick group significantly above a no-lick group:",
          bool(((four["KW p"] < 0.05) & (four["lick > no lick pairs significant (of 9)"] > 0)).all()), "\n")

Result: not reproduced. At 1.2 to 1.4 s ALM, wM2, wS2 and wS1 each give Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.05 (0.0002, below 0.0001, below 0.0001, 0.0076) with lick groups significantly above no-lick groups, as the statement says, and A1 does not (p 0.40). But under both effect-size readings the largest effect is in wM2, not ALM: Cohen's d wM2 3.80, ALM 1.95, wS2 1.16, wS1 0.94; Kruskal-Wallis statistic wM2 49.2, wS2 27.3, ALM 24.5, wS1 15.8. The readings agree on the largest area, so the claim is not blocked; it fails on its ranking. The plain difference of the mean projections, which is not one of the criterion's readings, ranks ALM (0.46), wM2 (0.35), wS2 (0.18) and wS1 (0.11) in the paper's order; the Supplementary Fig. 18 legend, which the claims file did not read, ranks the areas by "the projection amplitude in the lick coding direction ... largest for ALM, followed by wM2, wS2 and wS1 (in rank order), with A1 having the smallest and not significant difference", which reads as this difference. Whether the claims file's effect size misreads the paper is asked of a reader (questions/ghaderi-2026.yaml). The code's quiet rule gives the same rankings.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. Quiet trials follow the Methods (median absolute deviation); the paper's code uses MATLAB's default mean absolute deviation, and with it the single-neuron fractions (Fig. 3c, 5a), the layer values (Fig. 3d) and the explained variances (Fig. 6a) come out at the paper's values, while with the Methods' rule they are lower. The 5 ms coding-direction analyses take their baseline and context window from the 10 ms counts. The lick coding direction uses the lick times and lick mask of the paper's Lick_times.mat with the dandiset's jaw trace, and its 1.2 to 1.4 s window comes from the 10 ms counts. Permutation and bootstrap seeds are fixed per section.

What was found about the dataset. The units, trials and unit counts per area are those of the paper; the optogenetic sessions per area are the paper's, but ALM inactivation comes from 7 mice where the Methods give 8; and the paper's cluster labels link one to one to the units. The genotype field of 12 optogenetic sessions (PG021, PG061) says C57BL/6JRj; one session has 11 trials of type 0; every session has at least one trial without video in its window, and two have many (243 and 29); several trial-table descriptions do not fit their columns; the area of a unit needs the CCF label list from the Zenodo record, which the dandiset does not hold.
